items.description: The Grand-Lahou lagoon relief is a dynamic coastal environment where the Bandama River enters the Atlantic. It is characterized by shifting sandbars and mangrove forests.
The Biankouma Massif is a rugged highland area in western Ivory Coast, part of the larger Guinea Highlands. It is known for its steep slopes and traditional Yacouba mountain villages.
The Bouake basin is a broad topographic depression in central Ivory Coast. It serves as a transitional zone between the northern savanna and the southern forest regions.
The San-Pedro coastal plain is a narrow strip of low-lying land in the southwest. It is defined by its rocky headlands, sandy bays, and proximity to the country's second-largest port.
The Fere savanna relief consists of open plains in the north-central part of the country. It is dominated by lateritic plateaus and seasonal watercourses known as marigots.
The Tiagba lagoon relief is a scenic section of the Ebrie lagoon system. It is famous for the village of Tiagba, where traditional houses are built on stilts above the water.
The Bongouanou plateau is a fertile upland area in south-central Ivory Coast. It is a key agricultural zone characterized by rolling hills and extensive cocoa plantations.
The Man Massif is the most prominent mountain range in western Ivory Coast, containing several peaks over 1,000 meters. The relief is marked by deep canyons and dramatic waterfalls.
The Yapo forest relief is a protected rainforest area situated on a low plateau near Agboville. It serves as a vital green lung and biodiversity corridor in the south.
The Bondoukou plain is a flat to gently undulating landscape in the east, near the border with Ghana. It is characterized by dry forest and savanna-parkland vegetation.
The Abidjan lagoon relief comprises the central part of the Ebrie Lagoon, which splits the city into northern and southern sectors. It is the defining geographical feature of the capital.
The Korhogo highlands form a series of low-rising plateaus and granite hills in the northern Senufo region. The relief is dotted with iconic inselbergs rising from the plains.
The N'zi river valley is a long, narrow depression that runs through central Ivory Coast. It is known for its fertile soils and seasonal flooding patterns that support agriculture.
The western Abidjan lagoon relief extends from the city toward the town of Dabou. It is a shallow, calm waterway lined with coconut groves and traditional fishing villages.
